title: Fourier phase mismatch exceeds fixed-shape controls in selected TESS CPV sector pairs
abstract: We test if changes in TESS complex periodic variable (CPV) dip templates admit one common phase shift. Our Fourier diagnostic allows each harmonic to change amplitude and uses no spot phase reference. We calibrate it with 300 fixed-template injections into real control stars. In orders 3-10, signal-supported good pairs include 1,253 pairs from 64 stars. Their equal-star fraction above the control-bin 95th percentile is 23.3% (95% resampling interval 8.8-37.6%). A strict shape-repeat cut gives 5.7% (0.0-16.0%) in 157 pairs from 44 stars. Orders 3-6 give similar results; orders 7-15 leave a larger strict-sample fraction of 14.1% (3.1-25.0%). Synthetic fixed-centre dips with changing depths can produce the mismatch without motion. Thus the test screens profile shifts before a transport interpretation. It does not identify material motion, dust or gas, or material life. Intervals include calibration threshold and star sampling uncertainty, but not source reduction errors. Coarse signal proxies, donor shape differences and shape-based selection limit inference. Original code, aggregate evidence, a figure, input hashes and separate-scratch repeat steps are included.

display.caption: Spot-free Fourier phase mismatch and signal-bin calibrated above-threshold fractions. Intervals resample controls and CPV stars. The strict cut selects similar shapes and does not prove material motion.
